title: Record that the C1 Q feedback edge leaves the four-input row coupled.
body: ## Change and mathematical scope Scoped negative result for one named feedback edge, no new κ. In the published two-edge active feed, the second operator `C1 Q` lies outside the 8,281-policy family. With the first operator held at the published identity, and with no added call, the four-input row after query 4 is not autonomous. The autonomous row at that checkpoint is `[D1 Q^{-1}, 0, Q^{-1} C3 D1 D3, 0]`. The named replay has first coefficient `Q^{-1} C1 Q^{-1} C1 D1` and a nonzero second coefficient. Holding either published operator fixed, no element of the predecessor's group algebra on the other edge makes that row autonomous. The unique second edge that restores `D1 Q^{-1}` is the published `C1 Q^2`, and it keeps a nonzero second coefficient. This identity is scoped to those hypotheses. It is not an unrestricted impossibility: the pair `F1 = Q` and `F2 = C1 Q`, both outside the family, does make the same row autonomous. That pair changes two edges. Its other final banks are not the four uncoded targets. The selected conditional κ remains `781451/250000000`. ## Task and overlap Base: `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`, priority revision 8. Card: `joint-query-controller`, scope **refined**. This does not change the query demand. It answers the second open question of the declared-family coupling note (fork draft PR 152), the remainder of handoff [discussion comment 19138525](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19138525) after `research/coded-active-feedback` restored the missing coefficient. The first open question of that note, an owner-indexed map on intact endpoint banks, is not taken. Live inputs: `research/coded-active-feedback/search.py` and `research/coded-native-caller/gauge.py`. Nearest work is that package. Overlap at this base covered 885 open upstream PRs and 6934 discussion records. No open upstream PR title states this named edge. The declared alternating-decoder lock does not change a feedback operator. ## Validation ```sh python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/active-feedback-outside-edge ``` Python 3.12, standard library only. Normal and optimized registered commands both print `PASS_ACTIVE_FEEDBACK_OUTSIDE_EDGE`. The optimized run still executes the checks. Controls: the named operator is outside the 91 second-edge choices; the published operator is inside; omitting the second edge does not restore `A`; the two-edge witness clears the row and does not clear the four final banks. Not run: a port-dependent map, a new feedback source, an added call, native tape, precision, compiler, outer admission, and any selected replay. The algebra is the predecessor's sufficient identity model. ## Credit Schedule, algebra, and policy family: Cinna Davis, `research/coded-active-feedback`, using Dugongue's PR4948 chronology, Dillon's PR4933 code, and the passive ceiling packaged by Chris R / Clear1nsight. Gauge engine: inherited `research/coded-native-caller/gauge.py`. The decoder-family question that left this edge is fork draft PR 152. Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Apache-2.0. ## Open next questions What ordinary bill does the two-edge witness `F1 = Q`, `F2 = C1 Q` pay, and which final banks can the existing scalar suffix clear? First compare those monomials with the published `I` and `C1 Q^2` on the same owned banks, then read final banks 0 and 3, before adding a call. Does one saved-bank source other than response2 make this row autonomous while the second operator stays `C1 Q^2`? Name that bank and the one operator added into the existing final-query argument. ## Workflow feedback (optional) The useful remainder was one named edge on the existing row, tested before any added call. The one-edge identities are sharp because the two-edge witness is recorded separately. Link once to the [feedback discussion](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1200).
